reports.shown:
Six runs on this commit, three per arm, each with a 300 s deadline, scripted pad input with a frame classifier, and frame dumps every tenth frame (APS5_DUMP_FRAMES=5400, APS5_DUMP_FRAMES_EVERY=10). Every run booted, loaded the save, reached the hub, walked to an NPC, closed a conversation, walked into the training area and landed attacks. All six passed every milestone, exited 0, and no log line matched SIGSEGV, abort, fatal, assert or Error:.

- **Original executable, 512 MiB upload pool: 3 of 3 runs.** ap-m17-01, ap-m17b-01, ap-m17b-02. - **Same with the 768 MiB upload pool: 3 of 3 runs.** ap-m17p3-01, ap-m17p3-02, ap-m17p3-03. The byte patch is the one #6206 proposes for the relinker patch file and #6314 implements; main does not have that mechanism, so it was written into app.elf by hand (one byte at file 0x290414, 0x20000000 -> 0x30000000).

So the pool patch is not needed for this route on this machine: 3 of 3 without it. That is not a proof that it is unnecessary in general — it is one host, one save, one route, and three runs.

Two earlier attempts on the patched directory failed in my test runner before the game was started (0.1 s), so they count for nothing here and were replaced by ap-m17p3-*.

**Shader caches.** One run per arm started with no cache entries for this build's key and wrote them (0 hits, 191 misses, 191 writes); it booted and reached the hub like the others. The other two runs per arm read the cache (189 to 191 hits, 0 misses). So the cold-start upload-pool overflow this thread describes did not reproduce in these two cold runs. That is one cold start per arm, not a claim that cold starts are fixed.

**What the scripted play reached**, in seconds from the start of the scripted input (a few seconds after launch) for ap-m17b-01: title 16.9, save select 20.8, hub 30.9, NPC prompt 37.6, conversation closed 51.0, training area 78.8, first landed hit 81.3. Across the six runs the hub came at 28.7-32.3 s, the closed conversation at 48.8-51.9 s and the first hit at 81.0-91.0 s. A hit is the game's own hit-point and hit counter, read by an added game script (see How it was run), not a picture: the dummy's hit points fell 1320 -> 1260 with hits: 3 in ap-m17b-01.

**Frame rate.** The rate is the fps field of the present lines, which is the rate the window title shows: a two-second window, one line after the first present and every 30 presents after that. It is not a per-frame interval. Each cell is the mean over the present lines of the scripted state in that run.

reports.shown: 4.7 -> 6.4-6.7 fps in the menu, median frame 198 ms -> 134 ms. GPU time is only ~28 ms per frame (APS5_PROFILE_GPU=1); the CPU queue thread is the limit. Per 10 s on that thread: draw capture walk ~2 s, Graphics::Draw ~2.4 s, image tables ~1.1 s, WAIT_REG_MEM ~1.5 s.

reports.author: Nesyth
reports.blockerText:
| | Blocker | Seen |
|---|---|---|
| B | Performance: CPU-bound on the queue 0 packet thread (see the notes under this table). | Every launch |
| G | One light is missing on a house on the left of the main menu, compared with the PS5. | Every launch |

Notes on blocker B, per frame at the station on the build above, with the profiler:
- Queue 0 takes about 170 ms per frame and the host GPU about 96 ms, so the frame waits on the CPU. About 1,400 draws per frame, most of them cached; a cached draw still costs about 33 µs, so about 42 ms per frame.
- With the draw pipeline of #1201/#1202 on, the title froze in both runs I made, the first about 25 s into the station. About 740 `EVENT_WRITE` packets per frame keep draining that pipeline. I'll put the details on #1202.
- The GPU's most expensive program (about 21 ms per frame) is mostly f16 math emulated with integer operations.
- Turning Lumen GI off (`r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod=0` in `engine.ini`) makes the station about 30 % faster.

Fixed since the first post:
- **A, lighting** (black silhouettes, missing city lights, black logo and menu text): gone after merging #3864, #3865, #4012 and #4248 locally; the same build without them stayed black. Not bisected.
  - #4012 (the zero dword fill kernel handled as a buffer fill) is the likely fix, so this looks like a DCC key race.
  - A related race, where a sampled texture read its keys before the GPU writes recorded ahead of it, is fixed by #4554, merged with the `0xff` key case I raised there.
- **C, comp-to-single DCC keys read as stored:** #4700.
- **D, the settings file abort:** #5255 (open) zero-fills short APR reads that reach the end of the file.
  - Ready or Not keeps the size its boot resolve returned (`sceKernelAprResolveFilepathsToIdsAndFileSizes`). It then rewrites `gameusersettings.ini` one byte shorter and reads it back with the old size, so `main` throws on the short read and the title aborts.
  - Confirmed on Linux by coltken95.

reports.shown:
Three launches, all exit code 0, no crash, no fatal line, and no error line other than the game's own ioerror_assets_all.bundle probe. The save directory was restored to its pre-run sha1 afterwards.

- Run 1, cold shader cache, frame dumps on: title "Press X to continue" by 15 s, cross to the main menu (Pilgrimage/Options/Credits), cross to SELECT PILGRIMAGE, cross on 1 New Game, black load then the intro cutscene from about 160 s, gameplay (HUD, health bar, sarcophagus with a triangle prompt) at about 385 s. Square, cross and left-stick presses followed (whether they moved or attacked is not visible, see Input); triangle opened the "Bile Flasks" tutorial modal. - Runs 2 and 3, warm cache, identical replays, frame dumps off: the present rate is 59.94 in the title, intro, 60 s play and 60 s idle windows (59.88–59.91 in the menus). Both runs produced 1166 present lines and reached present n 34950.

The fps values are the fps field of the present lines in videoout.jsonl, which is the rate the window title shows (a two-second window, written after the first present and every 30 presents). Phase windows for the two dump-free runs rest on log anchors (first press, the intro loader line cutscenesvideos_assets_cts01.mp4.bundle) plus run 1's timing, not on pixels.

| phase | r2 mean | r3 mean | r2 min | r3 min | lines each | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | boot (0-30 s) | 54.17 | 54.41 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 56 | | title screen | 59.94 | 59.94 | 59.92 | 59.91 | 180 | | main menu + slot select | 59.91 | 59.88 | 59.44 | 58.95 | 64 | | load + intro cutscene | 59.94 | 59.94 | 59.88 | 59.87 | 448 | | gameplay, 60 s scripted play | 59.94 | 59.94 | 59.93 | 59.89 | 120 | | gameplay, 60 s idle | 59.94 | 59.94 | 59.92 | 59.88 | 120 |

Cold run, same measure: title screen 59.88 mean (212 lines, 15-121.5 s), load and intro 59.73 mean with a 49.46 minimum (463 lines, 160-385 s), scripted play 59.94.

**Shader caches.** Run 1 was cold and wrote them: 0 hits, 228 misses, 228 writes. Runs 2 and 3 read all of them: 228 hits, 0 misses, 0 writes. Time from launch to the intro loader line: 160 s in the cold run (read off the one-per-second dumps, +-2 s) and 166.3 s in both warm runs.

**New Game load.** The only stall after boot is at the New Game load: 0.768 s and 0.734 s in run 1, a single 0.751 s and 0.738 s interval in runs 2 and 3 (30 frames, i.e. 39-41 frames a second by 30/interval). The reported rate then dips from 59.94 to 54.46 (run 2) and 54.52 (run 3) and is back at 59.96 after 210 frames, about 3.5 s.

**Continue was not tested, and this title did not offer a Continue entry.** With the 2026-10-11 _sd/slot0 save in place, the title screen goes straight to the main menu and the slot list shows only 1 New Game, 2 [Empty], 3 [Empty]; the game added a 3-byte _sd/slot0.blocks when it probed that save. So the 0.26 s stall after a continue-load that the Windows report describes could not be reproduced or contradicted here: that save was never a valid in-game save.

**Input** was scripted with APS5_PAD_INPUT_FILE (a pad command file written before each launch and replayed by the emulator): 3 menu crosses plus a 17-entry square/cross/left-stick script in each of runs 2 and 3, all of which fired on schedule. Whether the walk distance and the attacks took effect in the opening room is not verified: the room uses a fixed camera and the dumps are 480x270, so the presses are shown to reach the game by the screen changes (menu navigation, tutorial modal) rather than by movement.

**Audio is not verified.** No audio capture was taken, so nothing is claimed about sound.
reports.blockerText:
None found. No fatal line, and no error line other than the game's own `ioerror_assets_all.bundle` probe; no crash in three launches.

One limitation of the telemetry, not of the game: no `pad` line was written in any of the three runs, although the scripted presses acted. `pad` lines carry the controller and keyboard/mouse state read through SDL, and `APS5_PAD_INPUT_FILE` input is applied later in `libScePad`, so file-injected input does not appear in them; a `pad` line needs a physical controller or host keyboard/mouse input.

- #5372: joining every memory range crossed by a bound buffer.
- #6364: storing pending image results after their writers finish.
- #6678: avoiding waits for small Windows imports.
- #6095: compiling resource-plan walks.

This is the tested stack, not an independently established minimum. The #5372 integration uses an earlier tested revision rather than its current PR head.

Local changes still include:

- Watched-private-import publication and retirement fixes, preserving GPU completion before backing memory is retired.
- Preservation of active outer images during nested refreshes.
- Complete-overwrite tracking that preserves CPU edits and accounts for subsequent writes.
- Staging estimates based on each shader invocation's write footprint.
- Carried correctness fixes for blending, image-view usage, CMASK synchronization, and LDS-lock initialization.

Remaining issues:

- Gameplay performance remains approximately 3–3.5 FPS in the tested scene.
- Puddles and distant terrain intermittently disappear. This also occurs on earlier control builds and predates the recent performance changes. Quality mode has not been established to fix it.
- Shader preparation can cause lengthy startup/loading pauses.
- Later areas, cinematics, and long-session stability remain untested.

reports.shown:
The first retail PS4 game in game on AnyPS5.

- Title screen, main menu and the opening forest, rendered correctly (fog, film grain, depth, silhouettes). - 57-58 fps in game (573-578 presents per 10 s against the 59.94 Hz vblank), at the game's normal speed, with about 12 ms of GPU work per frame on an RTX 5060 Ti. - Sound plays: one AudioOut port, 48 kHz stereo float, consumed in real time. - Input works: the menu responds and the boy walks, with the keyboard and with APS5_PAD_INPUT_FILE. - Not tried yet: a full playthrough, saving and loading across sessions, Linux, macOS, AMD and Intel GPUs.

The values were equal, but the gameplay advanced about half as far per frame (slow motion), which showed on 17 Oct when every frame was dumped under the same input and save. The numbers above are with those clears running the real kernel.

How it got here, for anyone bringing up the next PS4 title: - **Convert:** main's relinker converts the eboot and the bundled libc.prx. Its jump tables and zero-length unwind records are handled since #6595 and #6619. The bundled libSceFios2.prx also needed #9429 (merged), for TLS relocations against the module's own section symbol. - **GPU without a second recompiler:** each GCN instruction is re-encoded to RDNA and decoded by the existing recompiler (#9430). A new libSceGnmDriver writes real PS4 packets and submits them to the AGC executor (#9432). - **PS4 memory layouts:** V# and T# descriptors are converted to the PS5 layout (#9430). The PS4 tile modes (thin, display, depth tile split, PRT) are in the GPU detiler as XOR equations, checked against addrlib's formulas (#9431). - **The bugs that took longest:** - A GCN V# base is 44 bits. Limbo leaves 0x7 in bits 47:44, which made gameplay white. - A 1920x1080 render target is really 1920x1088, which cost a round trip through guest memory every frame (42 fps) until it became a GPU copy. - The two-dword clears above. - **Outside the GPU:** PS4 NpTrophy, save data v1, NpWebApi offline and Limbo's other imports (#9433, merged), with sceNpSetContentRestriction from #9225 (merged).

reports.shown:
The menu works and save slots are found. New Game loads (slowly), and the title is playable in game: the level renders, the player can move, and the cutscenes play. Keyboard and mouse work in the menus and in game, and audio works.

Frame rate in game: 1 to 2 FPS. With APS5_PROFILE_DRAW=1 APS5_PROFILE_GPU=1: - 1.8 FPS without the draw-input patch below. This run crashed in the second cutscene (see "Current blocker"). - 2.4 FPS with it. This run got past the second cutscene and was closed by hand.

No NotImplemented stop, no unresolved import, no missing function in any run.

Where the time goes (run with the patch, 10 s window in game, APS5_PROFILE_DRAW=1): - Queue 0 is CPU-bound. Draw packets take 9.5 s of every 10 s: 49,474 draws at 193 µs each (295 µs without the patch). The GPU is about 10 % busy. - readTarget takes 2.9 s per 10 s, over 89,216 resident target lookups (88,136 with a partial scissor, 1,080 full). 648 of these lookups take 1 ms or more, 1.6 s in total. - lookup takes 3.4 s per 10 s. [rescache] shows 1,393 hits against 36,522 misses, of which 18,387 are "same key (not inserted or evicted)". [textures] stage A shows 1 fast hit against 298,729 full lookups.

The slow target lookups compare untracked memory byte by byte. At startup the log says [write-watch] Windows direct host imports use comparisons; separate shared aliases retain guest write tracking.

In the main menu without input, after about 80 s, the draw time is dominated by the same path: 1,872 lookups of 1 ms or more take 4.2 s of 7.8 s. A worker sample of that phase (APS5_SAMPLE_WORKER, steady-state difference of two snapshots) shows: - 52.7 % self time in ucrtbase (memcmp and memcpy). - StorageTexture::Refresh: 86 % inclusive. Inside it: - compareUntracked → GuestMemory::EqualsCommittedUnsynced: 27.5 %. - upload → captureGuestBytes → ReadCommittedUnsynced: 25 %.

The render targets appear to sit in host-imported memory, so every refresh in a new collect epoch compares the whole surface (about 33 MB for a 3840×2160 target, about 2 ms). When the GPU has written it back, the surface is also captured and uploaded again. The comparedGuestBytes memo only holds within one epoch unless the range is hinted, and the queue bumps the epoch about 40 times per frame here.

Experiments in the menu: - APS5_NO_HOST_IMPORT=1 removes the compares (readTarget 71 ms), but the menu drops from about 10.7 to 1.5 presents/s. - APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB=1024 aborts with an address-based build copies 891 MiB of 4627 registered ranges, past 64 MiB (APS5_ADDRESS_COPY_MAX_MIB).

reports.blockerText:
The stop: AK::EventManager reads out of bounds, at the prison area after the tutorial boss.
It reproduced in 2 of 2 runs, at the same instruction:

```
FATAL: unhandled exception 0xc0000005 on thread 'AK::EventManager'
  rip AkSoundEngine.prx.guest.prx+0x180e57
  read of 0x0000000000001ffc     (run 1)
  read of 0x00000000000027fc     (run 2)
```

```
#0 AkSoundEngine+0x19c8ca   #5 AkSoundEngine+0x17a588
#1 AkSoundEngine+0x19aa5f   #6 AkSoundEngine+0x1a3f7d
#2 AkSoundEngine+0x17a40a   #7 AkSoundEngine+0xc4981
#3 AkSoundEngine+0x17b755   #8 AkSoundEngine+0x1a35e3
#4 AkSoundEngine+0x17ab9a   #9 libkernel+0x516a6
```

The faulting address moves between runs though. Both reads are limit − 4 (0x2000 − 4 and 0x2800 − 4), with r10 carrying the limit (0x1800, 0x2000) and rdx = r8 = r9 = 0x200 constant. So the same instruction walks off the end of a live object by one element, and the distance depends on state — not a fixed bad pointer.

This looks like the third title to hit it.
- Resident Evil Village #5169 — "the Wwise thread AK::EventManager hit an access violation walking a list whose record has every qword shifted by 4 bytes."
- Onimusha: Way of the Sword #6046 — same thread, same failure. Closed as fixed, on the report that it no longer reproduced on main 0afa6a607. "I haven't bisected which change in between removed it."

Furi runs ea5c27b53, which is 774 commits past that base, and still crashes the same way. So whatever removed it for Onimusha wasn't a fix.

Cause is likely known. #6046's comments identify this as a use-after-free: a Wwise voice object is freed, its memory reused for a stereo pan gain (0x70710677 pair), and the voice still points at it. The suspected mechanism is libSceAcm being a no-op — sceAcmBatchWait returns instantly, so a batch object can be freed before the batch would really have completed. Worth noting the AudioOut2 pacing there too: real time needs ~47 pushes/s, observed 0.4 to 7.2/s.

Its OpenTelemetry exporter sends its first trace batch then, as an HTTP/1.1 POST to an HTTPS server. With #11611 the request goes out but the title stops at 65 s on `sceHttp2: TLS failed; console error mapping is unknown`, because the server's certificate cannot be verified. With #11611 and either #11145 (system certificate roots: the POSTs then complete with 200) or #11922 (the failed handshake returns `0x8095F00C`, as on a PS5, and the exporter retries every 31 s), the title runs to a 600 s limit without stopping.

```
FAIL: Forbidden syscall instruction at code offset 0x129f1c (offset 0x129f1c)
Input: ...\eboot.bin
```

The offset is in `Media/Modules/MonoAssembliesPS4.prx`, the Mono AOT image. Its executable segment runs from 0x0 to 0x2ddf930, but `.eh_frame_hdr` lists only 3 FDEs, all at the end of that segment: 0x2ddf300..0x2ddf7a5, 0x2ddf7b0..0x2ddf7db and 0x2ddf7e0..0x2ddf7ed. The AOT-compiled methods have no DWARF unwind entries. Unwind ranges therefore cannot bound the code, and the data inside the executable segment is scanned as instructions. The bytes around 0x129f1c (`09052a00f8040000000028010f05c400`) look like table data. The executable segment contains 436 `0F 05` byte pairs in total.

Needed: a way to bound the code of a Mono AOT module, or to tell its data from its code. Open pull requests still needed: #6684, #7660 and the TLS fix in #6977. #6977 is also needed to run the title.

title: Assassin's Creed Shadows (PPSA20397): boot cinematics render, stops at the stencil replay-safety gate

reports.author: akkadbakkad89
reports.build: main 2185dbf92 plus the feat/psml-mfsr-queries branch commits (the psml MFSR exports of #8290) and the libSceNpGameIntent app-launcher lifecycle of #8355. Windows build of that tree, all runtime libraries one vintage.
reports.shown:
The window presents real rendered frames: an in-engine cinematic (character tumble through the bright chamber), the AC logo over the sky backdrop, and the "This game saves data automatically" notice. The title bar frame counter climbs past 1,300 at ~25 FPS. About 9,000-9,300 shaders compile on a cold run; texture streaming/detiling and save-journal writes continue until the abort.

![In-engine cinematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akkadbakkad89/AnyPS5/game-assets/acs/cinematic.png)

![Assassin's Creed logo splash](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akkadbakkad89/AnyPS5/game-assets/acs/logo.png)

![Auto-save notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akkadbakkad89/AnyPS5/game-assets/acs/autosave.png)
reports.blockerText:
A presentation draw aborts the run on this GPU:

```
shader 0x407325e400 stage 5: ShaderRecompiler::Recompile:
stencil reference export emulation requires a replay-safe pixel shader with late tests
[videoout] presentation failed
```

The draw writes stencil unconditionally (front+back compare `ALWAYS`, all ops `REPLACE`, masks `0xff`) at 4xMSAA with a reference exported per pixel. That reference is a texture-derived value (`ImageRead`), so it is unbounded: on a device without `VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export` the recompiler takes the all-256-value replay path, but the shader then fails `StencilReplaySafe` — `maskStable()` cannot prove the `Ballot`/`WqmU64` helper-lane mask stable across replays — and the draw also trips the `samples == 1` replay gate. Full shader/draw analysis is in #8514.

Resolved along the way: the early-boot dead-handle SIGSEGV of #8514 was a launch-subset content artifact — a forge pack absent from the partial `app0/` populated the handle-table slot. With the complete image it never reproduces.

reports.blockerText:
An intermittent abort about 2 s after start: `sceKernelWaitSema: invalid argument` (1 of 14 clean starts; never under GDB).

Cause, from the executable: the init function at `0x44xx` starts a worker thread (entry `0x48d0`) before it calls `sceKernelCreateSema(&sem /* 0x1fc0a8 */, ..., attr 1, init 0, max 1)` at `0x4506`. The worker loop at `0x4a06` calls `sceKernelWaitSema(sem, 1, NULL)` and, on a non-zero result, prints an error and loops back. When the worker runs first, it passes a null handle and expects an error it can retry, but `sceKernelWaitSema` throws on a null handle.

The fix (PR linked below) returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_ESRCH` for a null handle, as shadPS4 does for an unallocated handle. With it, a 180 s run and 8 starts showed no stop.

reports.blockerText:
None on AMD RDNA hardware (playable in game at 60 FPS).

Blockers on NVIDIA / 32-wide subgroup hardware:
1. **Wave64 in deferred shading**: Fragment shaders running on 32-lane subgroups clamp cross-lane operations (`SpirvAluEmitterMath.cpp`), causing UE4's cascaded shadow projection and directional lighting evaluation to collapse to zero for opaque G-Buffer passes.
2. **PCIe host-import latency**: As noted in architecture documentation, host imports of guest memory on NVIDIA's Windows driver incur substantial read stalls during draw submission, capping throughput at single-digit FPS.

reports.author: thuanquang
reports.shown: - On main it boots and presents frames, then stops at the title's first trophy query. The trophy file has IDs 0 to 18, and the title asks for 19: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument' what(): sceNpTrophy2GetTrophyInfo: trophy 19 is not in /app0/sce_sys/trophy2/trophy00.ucp FATAL: abort() (SIGABRT) - With #9115 (on main 3e91c8edf5 and 2f161d4f33), there is no stop in 10-minute runs. The Terms of Use, the title screen, Game Selection and the launcher menus render correctly at 50-60 fps. So do METAL GEAR SOLID's (the PS1 game's) boot logos, opening and codec calls. - With #9115 alone, MGS1 runs at about 4-8 fps, with dips to 1.5-2 fps. About half of its draws go into three linear 3072x2048 RGBA8 color targets that no host import covers, so they are synchronous: each reads its target from guest memory and stores it back, 17-21 ms per draw. At that speed, Snake does not get to move within 10 minutes. - With all four PRs on main 6ef5a1c4c9 (2026-10-22, one 600 s run, scripted input, no local changes), MGS1 reaches gameplay: the launcher, the Start Menu, MGS1's title, SELECT GAME LEVEL, the opening and the codec call, then the Dock with the radar and the opening credits, from about 250-280 s on. There is no stop in the run. - The launcher runs at 55-60 fps. The opening and codec run at 17 fps, the Dock at 18-21 fps. - Movement was not tested. - With local changes, not PRs, MGS1 plays at the Dock at 59-60 fps: the targets are imported, and they are stored back less often than after every draw. VR Missions plays too. On those builds no other stop was found in the launcher, the Master Book, Options, MGS1 or VR Missions. - Input works through APS5_PAD_INPUT_FILE. - Audio plays. In MGS1's PS1 part at 17-21 fps it sounds choppy. The title's one AudioOut port (48 kHz, 8 channels, 256 samples per buffer, fed by sceNgs2SystemRender) gets 1.000 s of audio per second there, and its queue never empties, so that queue is not what drops. The cause is not known yet.
reports.blockerText:
- The trophy stop: #9115.
- MGS1's speed:
  - #9188 returns a synchronous draw's render target memory to the image pool.
  - #9202 stores only the bytes a synchronous draw changed in a linear target.
  - Together they take a synchronous draw from 16-50 ms to about 1.8 ms. On equal content, aligned by guest flip count, MGS1's boot logos go from 10.7-21.4 to 30.3-52.8 flips/s.
  - #9217 asks which store-back rule is acceptable for resident linear targets, with the local numbers. MarcZX10's answer there: keep the store guarantee, and speed up the synchronous path.
- Frame-time measurement: #9373 and #9602 move `APS5_PROFILE_DRAW`'s draw reports and the frame-dump log line to the asynchronous profile output. As synchronous writes to stderr, they added hitches of up to 208 ms.

Performance, not a stop. Two things bound the frame on this `main`:

- CPU copies of buffers outside the host imports: 1.55 GiB per 10 s window (25.9 GB over the run, 22.9 GB of it from the region at 0x2050000000), about 2.5 s of every 10 s on queue worker 0. This is the case #5372 removes (open, conflicting with `main`): with it merged locally on `main` 4b462ef60 the copies were zero, GPU busy per present 75 to 83 ms and the frame 171 ms at the median.
- The draw committer thread: about 40,000 draw packets per 10 s at 77 to 86 µs each (capture 18.6, recompile lookup 19.2, lock wait 20.1 µs per draw), the problem #7895 tracks. The draw cache hits 0.0 % of draws in gameplay: 97 % of the misses are draws whose only difference is per-draw pointers in the user data (#4054), and relocation (#4943) does not reach them because every vertex stage reads its fetch tables through such pointers and the vertex shaders build their buffer descriptors from the pointer words; on local prototypes stacked on #5609 and #6539 the hit rate stays at 0.5 to 0.7 % because the per-stage alias is keyed on SRT contents that differ per draw. The counters will follow as a comment for the owners of #5609 and #6539.

GPU time per present on this run (`APS5_PROFILE_GPU=1`, program ranges): 0x200fae0000 20.1 ms over 8 dispatches, 0x2013ba0000 12.6 ms, 0x206fd50000 9.8 ms, 0x200e480000 6.2 ms, the skin-cache kernel 0x200fa10000 4.8 ms over 15 dispatches with #8336 (55 ms without it: its 2.5 and 3.3 MiB outputs were written in place into the host import at 4.2 ms per dispatch).

reports.shown:
The probe menu shows and the runtime constructors run (Runtime constructors: 359; page size: 16384 bytes). The core image opens. Picking the first row stops inside JNI_CreateJavaVM, while HotSpot protects the main thread's stack guard pages:

STAGE: Calling real JNI_CreateJavaVM [0.404s][warning][os,thread] Attempt to protect stack guard pages failed (0x00007fffff7ff000-0x00007fffff80b000).

hs_err_java25_*.log:

# Native memory allocation (mprotect) failed to protect 49152 bytes. Error detail: memory to guard stack pages # Internal Error (stackOverflow.cpp:113), pid=114037, tid=100001

While writing that report, the VM reads kern.boottime, and the process ends with:

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error' what(): sysctl_nid_postfix: unsupported MIB 1.21
reports.blockerText:
On Linux, the thread stacks that `scePthreadAttrGet` / `pthread_attr_get_np` / `sceKernelIsStack` report do not start on a 16 KiB page boundary. HotSpot aligns its guard zone down to its 16 KiB page, so `mprotect` lands below the reported stack and is refused.

Open pull request: #9684 (aligns created and adopted thread stacks on Linux).

The same stop shows on Java 25 ZIP/JAR (PPSA99867, 01.000.000) and Java 25 Dependencies (PPSA99873, 01.000.001) from the same project. With the fix, all three titles pass every row, and the VM is created and destroyed.

reports.build: main d6eafa54d with #9694 (793e51a91).
reports.shown: - The opening menus render: language, brightness, adjustments, the photosensitivity warning, the autosave notice, then the title screen and main menu. - New Game loads into the prologue. You can pick up and inspect objects, and button prompts show. It finishes the prologue and starts loading the next chapter (the Milano). - First visits are slow on a cold cache: about 0.3–1 FPS while shaders and pipelines build, including one 1.7M-word compute shader. There are also long waits while level data streams in. The menus run at about 13–30 FPS once compiled. - **Fixed so far:** - The compute shader 0x3b91c3e00 stop at pc=0x4380 (#7362), fixed by #8991 (merged). - The first-level stop CB metadata pass over part of a color target: fast-clear eliminates over targets without CMASK or DCC under a leftover viewport scissor. #9694 fixes it (open). - **AMD:** on the V620 with RADV's default ACO compiler, the title crashes about 10 minutes after START GAME. The SIGSEGV is inside libvulkan_radeon.so, in aco::live_var_analysis, while it compiles a 731k-word fragment shader. It reproduces in a standalone pipeline-creation program, and the SPIR-V passes spirv-val. With RADV_DEBUG=llvm the same pipeline compiles, slowly, and the title reaches the warning screen. A reduced test case for a Mesa report is in progress. This is not an AnyPS5 defect.

One emulator-side problem shows when `/download0` cannot be used (it is created from the package's `sce_sys`, so a package without that directory has none, and a read-only location would do the same): the title's first `freopen` of `stdout` fails, which leaves the stream closed, and a later `freopen` of that closed stream aborts the process on `main`:

```
[libc] unhandled exception 'St13runtime_error' thrown from 0x7ffff5d4ddda
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  FileStream: closed stream
```

FreeBSD's `freopen` reopens a closed `FILE`, so the console carries on. The pull request below makes `freopen` do the same; with it the title runs through to its data check (exit 0) in that layout too. Pull request: #9763.

reports.build: main adca8cfa2f (2026-10-21) with open PRs #4449, #9551, #9989 and #6553 merged on top, plus local changes (listed under Current blocker). Plain main does not reach the menu on this system (see #9295).
reports.shown:
Shown in order: the SIE and Naughty Dog logos, the PlayStation intro video, the language menu, the title screen ("PRESS ANY BUTTON") and the main menu.

- The intro video plays at 59.94 fps. - The title screen and the menu run at about 0.7 fps (7 to 9 presents per 10 s; the GPU is busy 250 to 1000 ms per frame). - The title screen has a magenta and blue vertical band over its left half. - I did not start a new game: every run so far ended within 5 to 12 minutes (see below). - Audio and input not assessed beyond pressing a button at the title screen.
reports.blockerText:
Memory. On this system (8 GB VRAM, 32 GB RAM) the title runs out of memory 5 to 12 minutes in, on the title screen or menu. I stop it with a watchdog first, because when GTT reached 24 GB the whole PC froze once. In a 4-minute sample:

- GTT 15.5 to 16.5 GB:
  - about 12.3 GB is guest memory imported through dma-buf (#943 and #4449); the import budget of 12288 MiB is full;
  - about 2.1 GB is image mirrors;
  - the rest is storage textures placed in host memory once VRAM is full.
- The process's own anonymous memory is 3 to 5 GB; swap use grows to 1.4 GB.

Two things make it worse:

- **Storage-texture churn.** When VRAM is full, the storage-texture budget falls to its 512 MiB floor. An image-table element at the base of the 5.2 GB GPU pool (0x1180000000, 16384x16384 RGBA8, exactly 1 GiB) is then recreated hundreds of times. Every time it evicts the rest of the cache, which re-uploads 50 to 120 GB per 10 s. With `APS5_TEXTURE_CACHE_MIB=3072` that falls to 10 to 15 GB per 10 s, but fps does not change.
- **Large array textures.** Other large arrays are created repeatedly, for example 2560x1440 with 23 to 142 layers, 512x512x526 and 120x68x4097. I have not yet checked whether the shaders use all of these layers.

Local changes in this run (not proposed as fixes):

- Image views of 1 GiB or more are bound as absent when they run past their guest allocation or are 16k by 16k. 2D arrays over 512 MiB are cut to the slices that fit.
- `ShaderMemory::readWords` copies its lazy blocks through `process_vm_readv`. In 2 of 7 runs it crashed with SIGSEGV (SEGV_ACCERR) in `TableSnapshotter::ReadRuns`: an image-table read hit a page in Retail CPU memory (0x102a800000, 0x102e000000) that was no longer readable. My guess is that the title decommitted the page while a capture was reading it. I have not opened an issue for this yet.
- Earlier local work for this title (MEM_SEMAPHORE, 64-bit image atomics, S# chain): see #9295.

reports.blockerText:
None on `main` 21668cc9d8 with #11506: no abort, no `not implemented` throw and no label-wait timeout in 1800 s. The limit is speed, and it is not the GPU (busy about 33 ms of a 60 ms present in a traced 15 s in Helgen): compute queue 0x28 waits on a label from queue 0 at each of its submissions, its fill dispatches wait for the GPU before they run (297 of 297 submissions, about 3 s in 10 s), and about a fifth of its fills, of 16 and 64 MiB over 64 KiB registered pieces (larger than the 8 MiB import window), are written by the CPU after the device goes idle. #4449 removes the host import failures there (1084 to 0) without changing the speed.

Limiting the CPU fill's whole-device wait to the fill's range exposed a remaining label race: a queue's own reset of a label had not reached memory when its next wait read the old value, so queue 0x28 passed a wait early and the queues deadlocked on `0x112a800020`/`0x112a800b80` (3 of 3 runs). #13883 (merged) holds such a wait until the queue's own store lands; with it, 0 of 6 runs froze.

Stops on the way, each with the build that got past the one before it:
1. `NGS2: reverb channel conversion is not implemented`, 19 s after start: the reverb voice has 2 inputs and 8 outputs. Fixed by #10347 (merged).
2. The New Game loading screen hangs at 140 to 151 s: `ResourceMaterializer::ExtractPlan` → `MayDecide` walks a shared condition once per path for shader 0x122151a400. #11506.
3. `AGC graphics: guest cube texture descriptor holds fewer than 6 array slices (format 71, 512x512x5, type 11, tile 27, mips 0..0 of 1) (base array 0)` at 155 s: pixel shader 0x121ddc3d00 samples a cube whose descriptor holds five slices. Fixed by #11507 (merged).
4. The title stops presenting about 200 s after start, at the start of the cart ride, after `[gpu] queue 0x28 WAIT_REG_MEM at 0x112a800020 timed out after 1000ms` and the same on queue 0x0: a label store that queue 0x28 had already taken and reset released its next wait. Fixed by #12923 (merged).

With it, the title connects and sends its `initialize` request (`{"id":1,"method":"initialize",...,"clientInfo":{"name":"codex_ps5","title":"Codex PS5","version":"0.0.4"}}`). The same stop as #4399: Afterglow uses the ps5-opengl runtime, whose retirement wait gives up after about 2 s, while AnyPS5 builds the pipeline for the runtime's large pixel shader. reports.author: JJenkx
reports.shown:
**On main:** app.elf does not start.

./app.elf: error while loading shared libraries: PS4sceSystemServiceParamGetInt_plugin.prx: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

**With the workaround:** an empty shared library under that name, put on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This is a local test only, not a proposal. The title then renders a first-person interior: a lit hallway with a painting, a lamp and furniture. The run lasted until the scheduled close at 293 s, exit 0, at 55 to 60 FPS, with no driver failure.
reports.blockerText:
`Media/Modules/Il2CppUserAssemblies.prx` lists `PS4sceSystemServiceParamGetInt_plugin.prx` among its needed modules (`app.Il2CppUserAssemblies.prx.guest.prx.needed.json`), but:
- the package does not contain that file. The extraction was checked against every package member.
- the module imports no symbol from it. Its registry only has `libSceNet`, `libSceNetCtl`, `libSceRtc`, `libSceSystemService` and `libkernel`.

So the console evidently boots without it. The relinker treats every dependency that is not a guest module as a host library and keeps it as `DT_NEEDED`, so the Linux loader refuses to start. A simple "no imports from it" rule is not safe: across the 30-odd runtimes I have staged, host libraries such as `libkernel.prx`, `libSceAgcDriver.prx` and `libSceRtc.prx` often appear as dependencies with no matching imports. A correct rule also needs to know which host libraries exist, and the relinker can't know that at relink time when `--rpath` is `$ORIGIN/libs`. That is a relinker design question, so I am not proposing a change here.

reports.shown:
compute shader 0x21ecb9200: AGC graphics: a shader buffer access of 0x21fac1000+0x28000 overlaps multisampled color target 0x21fac1000+0x28000 (8 samples), whose samples are only on the host: guest access to it is not implemented

With #7002 applied, the same stop names the access as a write: a shader buffer write of 0x21fac1000+0x28000 …. The compute shader's buffer covers exactly the 0x28000 bytes of the 8-sample color target.
reports.blockerText:
A compute buffer write over a multisampled color target whose samples exist only on the host. These PRs, each merged alone onto the same `main`, give the same stop:

| PR | Merge |
|---|---|
| #7002, publish native color for read-only shader buffers | `01ec1d7a39` |
| #13248, claim a multisampled color target that a single-sample storage image store overlaps | `0fc12fa21a` |
| #13963, store storage results pending under a multisampled color target before it takes the memory | `2fbcc57b1f` |
| #10049, retire a multisampled color target a write-only storage image overwrites | `d538a6004c` |

Whether this write replaces the target's memory or reads it as well is not established from this run.
